_note: ABA-accredited law schools across the 12 shortlisted states. Median GPA/LSAT and in/out-state tuition are approximate recent-cycle public (ABA 509) values — a point-in-time snapshot; spot-check each school's official 509 before relying on it. 'tier' is a public-data proxy derived from selectivity/outcomes (we do not republish paywalled US News data). 'rank' is an approximate national rank where widely known, else null. All fields editable.

schools.name: Stanford Law School
schools.writeup: Elite nationally — unmatched for clerkships, academia, and tech/IP law given its Silicon Valley ties. Falls short only on cost: full private sticker with limited need-based aid.

schools.name: UC Berkeley School of Law
schools.writeup: T14 with deep pull in California and tech; strong public-interest and IP programs. Public 'discount' is modest — resident tuition is still high and Bay Area cost of living is brutal.

schools.name: UCLA School of Law
schools.writeup: Best launchpad into the LA market and entertainment law; strong across the board. Slightly weaker national portability than the T14 above it, but excellent value for a Californian.

schools.name: USC Gould School of Law
schools.writeup: Strong LA Big Law and entertainment placement with a tight alumni network. Private sticker is steep and it leans regional outside California.

schools.name: UC Irvine School of Law
schools.writeup: Young but fast-rising, well-regarded faculty and good SoCal placement. Still building national brand recognition.

schools.name: UC Davis School of Law
schools.writeup: Solid NorCal/Sacramento and public-sector placement with an environmental-law strength. Less national reach; better as an in-state value play.

schools.name: UC Law San Francisco
schools.writeup: Downtown SF location feeds Bay Area employers and litigation. Large class and thinner national portability drag on outcomes.

schools.name: Pepperdine Caruso School of Law
schools.writeup: Nationally ranked dispute-resolution program and improving outcomes. High private cost and a smaller regional network outside SoCal.

schools.name: Loyola Law School
schools.writeup: Deep LA litigation and public-interest pipeline with strong local alumni. Regional focus and private-school price tag.

schools.name: University of San Diego School of Law
schools.writeup: Best-connected school in the San Diego market. Outcomes are regional and cost is high for the ranking.

schools.name: Santa Clara University School of Law
schools.writeup: Silicon Valley location gives a genuine tech/IP edge. Otherwise regional with modest big-firm placement.

schools.name: Chapman University Fowler School of Law
schools.writeup: Growing Orange County school with improving bar numbers. Limited reach beyond SoCal.

schools.name: University of San Francisco School of Law
schools.writeup: Bay Area access and a social-justice bent. Weak big-firm placement and high cost relative to outcomes.

schools.name: Southwestern Law School
schools.writeup: Entertainment-law niche and a large LA network. Bar passage and employment lag; heavy debt risk at sticker.

schools.name: California Western School of Law
schools.writeup: Access-oriented San Diego school. Below-median bar passage and outcomes make cost the main concern.

schools.name: University of Texas School of Law
schools.writeup: The dominant firm-placement school in Texas and a national T20, with a huge Big Law pipeline into Houston/Dallas/Austin. In-state tuition makes it one of the best value-to-prestige plays in the country.

schools.name: Texas A&M School of Law
schools.writeup: The country's fastest riser — big scholarship money and improving outcomes on a low in-state tuition. Brand still catching up to its ranking; Fort Worth location is DFW-centric.

schools.name: SMU Dedman School of Law
schools.writeup: Best-connected school in the Dallas Big Law market with a strong local alumni base. Private cost and a regional (DFW) footprint are the tradeoffs.

schools.name: Baylor Law School
schools.writeup: Famous for producing trial-ready litigators and top-in-state bar passage. Grueling 'quarter' system and a small-town location aren't for everyone.

schools.name: University of Houston Law Center
schools.writeup: Strong, affordable in-state option feeding the huge Houston energy/corporate market. Outcomes are solid regionally but limited nationally.

schools.name: Texas Tech University School of Law
schools.writeup: Very affordable with reliable Texas bar passage and West Texas/regional placement. Isolated location and limited big-firm reach.

schools.name: St. Mary's University School of Law
schools.writeup: Anchors the San Antonio legal market with a strong local network. Bar and employment outcomes trail the state's public schools.

schools.name: South Texas College of Law Houston
schools.writeup: Nationally known advocacy/moot-court program and Houston access. Otherwise regional with middling outcomes at a private price.

schools.name: Texas Southern University Thurgood Marshall
schools.writeup: HBCU with a strong public-interest and diversity mission and low in-state cost. Bar passage volatility is the main risk.

schools.name: UNT Dallas College of Law
schools.writeup: The cheapest path to a Texas JD, built for access with a downtown Dallas location. Newer school still establishing its bar-passage track record.

schools.name: University of Chicago Law School
schools.writeup: Top-5 nationally — intellectually intense, elite for clerkships, academia, and Big Law anywhere. The cost is full sticker and the culture is famously rigorous.

schools.name: Northwestern Pritzker School of Law
schools.writeup: T14 with the strongest Big Law and corporate placement in Chicago and a business-minded, collegial culture. Values work experience in admissions; full private cost.

schools.name: University of Illinois College of Law
schools.writeup: Strong Chicago and Midwest placement at a relative discount, with good scholarship money. Champaign-Urbana location and a more regional pull than the Chicago T14s.

schools.name: Loyola University Chicago School of Law
schools.writeup: Well-regarded health-law and trial-advocacy programs with solid Chicago placement. Regional footprint and private cost.

schools.name: Chicago-Kent College of Law
schools.writeup: Strong legal-writing and IP/tech programs with downtown Chicago access. Middle-of-the-market outcomes at a high sticker.

schools.name: DePaul University College of Law
schools.writeup: Large Chicago alumni network and good part-time options. Employment outcomes are regional and cost is high for the tier.

schools.name: UIC School of Law
schools.writeup: Formerly John Marshall — deep Chicago practitioner network and IP strength. Bar and big-firm outcomes lag the city's stronger schools.

schools.name: Southern Illinois University School of Law
schools.writeup: Low in-state tuition and reliable downstate/central-Illinois placement. Limited reach into the Chicago market.

schools.name: Northern Illinois University College of Law
schools.writeup: Affordable public option with regional northern-Illinois placement. Small program with limited national profile.

schools.name: University of Michigan Law School
schools.writeup: A top national school that places into Big Law and clerkships in every major market, not just the Midwest. Nonresident tuition is nearly the same as resident — it's priced like a private.

schools.name: Michigan State University College of Law
schools.writeup: Now fully integrated into MSU with improving resources and solid Michigan placement. Outcomes are regional and the ranking has been volatile.

schools.name: Wayne State University Law School
schools.writeup: Best value in the Detroit metro with strong local firm and government placement. Limited pull outside Michigan.

schools.name: University of Detroit Mercy School of Law
schools.writeup: Detroit access plus a unique dual US/Canadian JD option. Private cost with regional outcomes.

schools.name: Western Michigan University Cooley Law School
schools.writeup: The most accessible admissions in the state — very high acceptance. Low bar passage and heavy debt make it a high-risk cost proposition.

schools.name: Harvard Law School
schools.writeup: The most recognized law degree in the world — opens any door, any market, any practice. Enormous class size means a less personal experience, and it's full sticker.

schools.name: Boston University School of Law
schools.writeup: T20 with excellent Boston and Northeast Big Law placement and standout tax/health-law programs. Strong but somewhat regionally concentrated outside the top markets.

schools.name: Boston College Law School
schools.writeup: Collegial culture with strong Boston firm and public-interest placement. Slightly suburban campus and a regional (Northeast) center of gravity.

schools.name: Northeastern University School of Law
schools.writeup: Distinctive co-op program gives real work experience before graduation; strong for public-interest careers. No traditional class rank/grades can complicate Big Law recruiting.

schools.name: Suffolk University Law School
schools.writeup: Huge Boston-area alumni network and strong evening/part-time options. Outcomes are regional and cost is high for the tier.

schools.name: New England Law Boston
schools.writeup: Downtown Boston access at an access-oriented admissions bar. Bar passage and employment outcomes lag.

schools.name: Western New England University School of Law
schools.writeup: Serves the western-Massachusetts/Connecticut-valley market. Small and regional with modest big-firm placement.

schools.name: UMass Law - Dartmouth
schools.writeup: The state's only public law school and by far the cheapest MA option. Newer, still building bar passage and its employment record.

schools.name: University of Maryland Francis King Carey
schools.writeup: Strong DC/Baltimore government, health-law, and public-interest placement at a reasonable in-state cost. National reach is limited beyond the mid-Atlantic.

schools.name: University of Baltimore School of Law
schools.writeup: Practical, practice-focused program with deep Baltimore and Maryland-government ties and strong part-time options. Outcomes are firmly regional.

schools.name: Duke University School of Law
schools.writeup: T14 with elite national placement, clerkships, and a famously supportive, non-cutthroat culture. It's a national school in a mid-size city — full private cost.

schools.name: UNC School of Law
schools.writeup: Outstanding value — in-state tuition with strong statewide and Southeast placement and a great campus town. Less national portability than Duke; nonresident cost is much higher.

schools.name: Wake Forest University School of Law
schools.writeup: Small, collegial program with solid North Carolina and Southeast firm placement. Regional reach and a private price tag.

schools.name: Campbell University School of Law
schools.writeup: Strong North Carolina bar passage and a downtown Raleigh location feeding state courts and firms. Regional profile with limited national pull.

schools.name: Elon University School of Law
schools.writeup: Accelerated 2.5-year option and experiential focus in the Piedmont Triad. Newer school still building its outcomes record.

schools.name: North Carolina Central University School of Law
schools.writeup: HBCU with a strong public-interest mission and the lowest in-state cost in the state. Bar passage variability is the main risk.

schools.name: University of South Carolina School of Law
schools.writeup: The dominant school in the SC legal market — deep ties to state courts, firms, and government, at a low in-state cost. Reach is almost entirely in-state; nonresident tuition erodes the value.

schools.name: Charleston School of Law
schools.writeup: Charleston location and local network for the Lowcountry market. For-profit history, higher cost, and weaker outcomes than USC.

schools.name: Vanderbilt Law School
schools.writeup: The South's premier national school — Big Law and clerkship placement across the country, plus a great Nashville quality of life. Full private sticker is the main tradeoff.

schools.name: University of Tennessee College of Law
schools.writeup: Excellent in-state value with strong Tennessee and regional placement and good bar passage. Limited national reach outside the Southeast.

schools.name: University of Memphis Cecil C. Humphreys
schools.writeup: Affordable public school anchoring the Memphis/Mid-South market. Outcomes are regional and the ranking sits well below UT.

schools.name: Belmont University College of Law
schools.writeup: Newer Nashville school with modern facilities and solid early bar numbers. Private cost and a still-developing alumni network.

schools.name: Lincoln Memorial University Duncan School of Law
schools.writeup: Access-oriented Knoxville school serving Appalachia. Lower entrance profile and outcomes; watch the debt-to-outcome ratio.

schools.name: Emory University School of Law
schools.writeup: Strong Atlanta and national Big Law placement with notable litigation and health-law programs. Full private cost and it competes hard with UGA for the Atlanta market.

schools.name: University of Georgia School of Law
schools.writeup: One of the best prestige-to-price ratios in the country — a T30 at deeply subsidized in-state tuition, dominant in Georgia. Nonresident cost is far higher and reach is Southeast-centric.

schools.name: Georgia State University College of Law
schools.writeup: Exceptional value — downtown Atlanta location, low in-state tuition, and strong government/firm placement in the metro. Regional footprint and a commuter feel.

schools.name: Mercer University School of Law
schools.writeup: Nationally recognized legal-writing program and strong central-Georgia placement. Regional and private-priced.

schools.name: Atlanta's John Marshall Law School
schools.writeup: Access-oriented Atlanta school with an evening program. Weak bar passage and outcomes make cost the central concern.

schools.name: University of Florida Levin College of Law
schools.writeup: The clear value leader in Florida — a T30 at low in-state tuition with the strongest statewide placement. Gainesville is a college town, and reach is mostly regional/Southeast.

schools.name: Florida State University College of Law
schools.writeup: Unbeatable for Florida government and policy careers given the Tallahassee capital location, at a low in-state cost. Less Big Law pull than UF and a regional footprint.

schools.name: University of Miami School of Law
schools.writeup: Largest alumni network in South Florida with strong Miami firm and international/Latin America placement. High private cost relative to outcomes.

schools.name: Florida International University College of Law
schools.writeup: Perennial #1 or #2 in Florida bar passage at a very low in-state cost — excellent value in the Miami market. Younger brand with mostly local reach.

schools.name: Stetson University College of Law
schools.writeup: Nationally top-ranked trial-advocacy program and strong Tampa Bay placement. Otherwise regional at a private price.

schools.name: Nova Southeastern University Shepard Broad
schools.writeup: Broward County access and a large South Florida network. Middling bar passage and outcomes for the cost.

schools.name: Florida A&M University College of Law
schools.writeup: HBCU with a strong diversity mission and the lowest in-state cost in Florida. Bar passage has been a persistent challenge.

schools.name: Barry University Dwayne O. Andreas School of Law
schools.writeup: Access-oriented Orlando school. Below-median outcomes; cost-to-outcome ratio warrants caution.

schools.name: St. Thomas University College of Law
schools.writeup: Miami access with a Catholic, public-interest mission and improving bar numbers. Regional with modest firm placement.

schools.name: Ave Maria School of Law
schools.writeup: Small, faith-based school on the Gulf coast. Limited network and regional-only outcomes.

schools.name: Columbia Law School
schools.writeup: T14 powerhouse with arguably the best Wall Street corporate and Big Law placement anywhere. Full sticker and an intense, large-market culture.

schools.name: New York University School of Law
schools.writeup: T14 with elite corporate, tax, and public-interest programs and unrivaled NYC placement. Enormous cost of attendance in the most expensive city in the country.

schools.name: Cornell Law School
schools.writeup: The smallest T14 — strong NYC Big Law placement with a close-knit culture. Isolated in upstate Ithaca, far from the market it feeds.

schools.name: Fordham University School of Law
schools.writeup: The best non-T14 pipeline into NYC Big Law and a massive, loyal Manhattan alumni network. Regionally concentrated and privately priced.

schools.name: Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law
schools.writeup: Strong NYC placement with standout IP, entertainment, and dispute-resolution programs. Reach is largely NYC-metro.

schools.name: St. John's University School of Law
schools.writeup: Strong NYC bar passage and a deep outer-borough/Long Island firm network. Regional footprint at a private cost.

schools.name: Brooklyn Law School
schools.writeup: Solid NYC placement with a large network and a strong corporate/BigLaw feeder history. Middle-market outcomes for a high sticker.

schools.name: University at Buffalo School of Law (SUNY)
schools.writeup: The best value in New York — SUNY tuition with dominant Western New York placement. Outcomes are heavily upstate/regional.

schools.name: Syracuse University College of Law
schools.writeup: Central New York placement plus a strong national-security/tech law niche and online options. Regional reach and private cost.

schools.name: Albany Law School
schools.writeup: Unbeatable for New York State government and capital-region careers given its Albany location. Regional footprint outside state government.

schools.name: Hofstra University Maurice A. Deane
schools.writeup: Long Island access and a strong trial-advocacy program. Regional outcomes at a high private cost.

schools.name: Pace University Elisabeth Haub School of Law
schools.writeup: The #1-ranked environmental-law program in the country and Westchester/NYC-suburb access. Otherwise regional.

schools.name: New York Law School
schools.writeup: Lower-Manhattan location and a large NYC network. Middle-market outcomes at a high sticker — not to be confused with NYU.

schools.name: CUNY School of Law
schools.writeup: The premier public-interest school in the country at the lowest tuition in NYC. By design it places into public-interest/government, not Big Law.

schools.name: Touro University Jacob D. Fuchsberg Law Center
schools.writeup: Long Island access with an access-oriented admissions bar. Bar passage and outcomes lag the cost.
